title: A ship-time MUST recorded only in a task note is invisible to closure: QCLI-433 closed with its DRIFT release-note mandate unmet
description:
Found during the 0.13.0 post-release correction (QCLI-467). QCLI-433 shipped 0.13.0 with a recorded MUST unmet: the note titled RELEASE NOTE FOR 0.13.0 on QCLI-433 (from opum-agent 2026-10-02, opum-doc ruling seq 167) reads "Must appear in the release notes when 0.13.0 ships, not only in the changelog", and 0.13.0 shipped with it in neither place.

WHY THE CHECKLIST PASSED IT. The mandate lives in implementationNotes. `quest task complete` warns only about unchecked acceptance criteria and definition-of-done items. The seven acceptance criteria on QCLI-433 cover the version sites, the six platform packages, the changelog section, the native receipt, the publish sequencing, the plugin and the landing -- NONE names the release notes or the note. So at completion there was nothing unchecked to trip the warning (the completion returned no unresolvedAtCompletion), and the final summary did not mention it either. A mandate written as prose in a note is invisible to the one mechanical check that closure runs.

WHAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, for the owner to choose rather than a guard built here:
1. Record a ship-time mandate as an acceptance criterion or a definition-of-done item at the moment it is recorded. QCLI-433 already had exactly that shape for the changelog entry -- "an explicit criterion below rather than a hope" -- so the pattern exists and was not applied to the release-note mandate. Then task complete warns, and the box cannot be checked without proof.
2. Have the release runbook step that cuts the release notes read the task notes for a required-note marker, so a MUST in prose is fetched at the moment it is needed rather than at filing time.
3. Product-side, quest could flag note text that reads as a directive at completion, but that is inference over prose; the first two are deterministic.

This is a finding, not a guard to build.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The record states the mechanism exactly: the mandate was an implementationNotes note on QCLI-433, quest task complete warns only about unchecked acceptance criteria and definition-of-done items, so a note-only MUST is silent at closure and no criterion existed to leave unchecked.
The record names what would have caught it and where the change belongs, leaving the choice to the owner rather than commissioning a guard here.
